summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of living donor liver transplant for primary sclerosing cholangitis presented with a week of abdominal discomfort, bloating, nausea, belching, and flatulence. Infectious workup including blood and urine cultures was negative, and CMV viral load was undetectable. Celiac serology showed no evidence of gluten exposure. Doppler ultrasound confirmed patent hepatic vasculature with normal flow. An upper endoscopy revealed normal mucosa with biopsies pending. Her immunosuppressive regimen was adjusted due to high tacrolimus levels and gastrointestinal intolerance: tacrolimus was reduced to 1.5 mg twice daily, and mycophenolate mofetil was switched to mycophenolate sodium. She was started on simethicone for symptom relief. With no acute findings and stable condition, she was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up to further evaluate the cause of her persistent abdominal symptoms.
